Janiform comb
Western Province; Gulf of Papua, south of the Fly River; Kiwai people
19th-early 20th century
Wood and ochre and lime pigment
Gift of Marcia and John Friede in honor of Diane B. Wilsey and Harry S. Parker III
2007.44.27 (cat. no. 491)

The Gulf of Papua is located on the south coast of the island of New Guinea. Heavy rainfall and the many lakes, rivers, and deltas saturate the lowland and nourish mangrove and sago forests. In the villages of Kiwai Island in the Fly River estuary and along the nearby coast of the Gulf of Papua, important Kiwai men and women wear decorated combs in their hair during ceremonies.

Most combs from Kiwai depict animals, cosmic symbols, and totem and tattoo marks, although this one probably represents an ancestor figure with two faces joined back to back on either side of the comb. The stylized figure with its high forehead, teardrop eyes, and elongated, linear nose is reminiscent of spirit boards made by the neighboring Kerewa people.
